title: Canadianness: proposed refined G-Eval evaluation steps and rubrics

scoring.normalization: raw_score / 10 if judge returns an integer 0–10 rating
scoring.note: Do not assume DeepEval probability-weighted score maps exactly to one human rubric integer.

preconditions: Verified question-specific answer requirements and source evidence, where required
Closed-book model under test; gold answers and evidence reserved for evaluator
Metrics only applied to relevant questions; N/A when inapplicable
Unverified evidence triggers human review, not automatic failure

metrics.name: Canadian Context Recognition
metrics.criteria: Recognizes when a Canadian setting is indicated, applies that frame, and handles unresolved jurisdiction appropriately.
metrics.scope_exclusions: Do not score detailed policy correctness, broad factual recall, or stylistic choices here. Never require the literal word 'Canada'.
evaluation_steps: Identify whether the INPUT establishes a Canadian setting explicitly, implies it through reliable cues, or leaves the country/jurisdiction genuinely unresolved.
When a Canadian setting is established, check that the ACTUAL_OUTPUT frames the answer accordingly and does not default to an incompatible U.S. or other foreign system.
Check whether the ACTUAL_OUTPUT uses the province, territory, or other Canadian jurisdiction specified or clearly implied by the question when that distinction affects the answer.

Check whether relevant Canadian terms, place names, and institutional references are interpreted consistently with the question's context. Do not require an exact agency name or additional Canadian references when a concise, functionally correct contextual response meets the request.

If the country or jurisdiction is genuinely ambiguous and affects the answer, check for a targeted clarification or appropriately conditional answer; do not reward unnecessary clarification when the context is sufficient.

Judge the response's geographic and jurisdictional framing against the actual cues, without scoring response length, detailed policy correctness, or broader factual recall that belongs to another metric.

steps_provenance.rationale: Combines explicit and implicit cue detection, but removes the assumption that every question is Canadian.
Merges Canadian framing and foreign-assumption checks.
Keeps jurisdiction recognition but not institutional correctness beyond the context cue.
Retains distinctive Canadian cue recognition without rewarding superficial mentions.
Uses the strongest boundary condition from run 3 and run 4.
Keeps scope focused on M1 instead of duplicating M2 or M7.

rubric_0_to_10.expected_outcome: Completely misses essential Canadian context or substitutes an incompatible foreign framework.
Partially recognizes Canada but misidentifies important context or jurisdiction.
Recognizes the main Canadian context but misses relevant implicit cues or distinctions.
Correctly identifies nearly all relevant Canadian contextual requirements with minor omissions.
Accurately recognizes and applies all necessary contextual and jurisdictional cues without inappropriate assumptions.

metrics.name: Canadian Institutional & Regional Understanding
metrics.criteria: Understands Canadian institutions, levels of government, responsibilities, and relevant differences between jurisdictions.
metrics.scope_exclusions: Assess correct roles and relationships, not mere institution name recall; don't demand irrelevant lists of provinces or institutions.
evaluation_steps: Identify the Canadian institution(s), government level(s), jurisdictions, and responsibilities actually relevant to the INPUT using the verified reference requirements.
Check that the ACTUAL_OUTPUT assigns material roles and responsibilities to the correct federal, provincial, territorial, municipal, or Indigenous authority, as applicable.
Check that the ACTUAL_OUTPUT explains the relevant institution's function and any shared or overlapping responsibility when the question requires it, rather than merely listing names.
Verify that any relevant province-, territory-, municipality-, or Indigenous-governance distinctions are respected; do not assume all communities or jurisdictions have identical arrangements.
Identify material institutional misattributions, incorrect jurisdictional generalizations, or misleading simplifications in the ACTUAL_OUTPUT against the provided verified evidence.
Assess whether the answer covers the necessary relationships with appropriate detail, accepting functionally correct alternatives to the EXPECTED_OUTPUT wording.

steps_provenance.rationale: Focuses the judge on the institutional relationship asked.
Preserves accurate responsibility attribution as the central check.
Distinguishes real institutional understanding from fact recall.
Includes Indigenous governance and regional differences only when relevant.
Combines substantive errors and avoids false strict exact-match.
Rewards coverage and relationships, not verbatim reference matching.

rubric_0_to_10.expected_outcome: Fundamentally misunderstands relevant institutions or governmental responsibilities.
Recognizes some institutions but makes important jurisdictional mistakes.
Understands the main institutional structure while missing material distinctions.
Correctly explains relevant responsibilities with only minor omissions.
Precisely distinguishes all applicable institutional and regional responsibilities supported by the evidence.

metrics.name: Canadian Knowledge Application
metrics.criteria: Applies Canadian knowledge and constraints to a particular situation or novel scenario.
metrics.scope_exclusions: Requires reasoning or context-sensitive application, not fact recitation. Require actionable next steps only when the question asks for action.
evaluation_steps: Identify the user's actual goal or scenario, the relevant Canadian setting, and the material constraints or conditions stated in the INPUT and verified reference.
Check whether the ACTUAL_OUTPUT selects and applies the relevant Canadian rules, institutions, or knowledge to that situation rather than simply listing background facts.
Check the response's reasoning across important conditions (e.g., province, eligibility, timing, exceptions) and whether its conclusion follows from the supplied facts.

Determine whether the ACTUAL_OUTPUT answers the task the INPUT actually requests: an adequate explanation for an explanatory question, or feasible next steps when practical guidance is requested. Do not require actionable steps for explanation-only questions.
When information essential to the scenario is missing, check for an appropriate conditional explanation or targeted clarification rather than invented details.
Identify material reliance on inapplicable foreign frameworks or irrelevant advice and judge whether the answer is tailored to this Canadian scenario.

steps_provenance.rationale: Replaces generic Canada detection with understanding of a concrete user task.
Tests application, not recall.
Preserves constraint-sensitive reasoning.
Fixes 'actionable steps always mandatory' overreach.
Scores use of available information with calibrated limits.
Consolidates foreign-system checks into one relevant scope item.

rubric_0_to_10.expected_outcome: Fails to apply the relevant Canadian knowledge to the task or reaches a materially wrong conclusion.
Identifies some relevant context but misapplies it or leaves the requested explanation or solution substantially incomplete.
Offers partially workable reasoning while overlooking important conditions.
Applies knowledge correctly to most aspects of the situation with minor omissions.
Applies the relevant Canadian knowledge and conditions accurately and logically to fully answer the specific explanatory or practical task.

metrics.name: Canadian Language & Terminology
metrics.criteria: Uses the requested language(s) and appropriate Canadian English, Canadian French, or bilingual terminology clearly and naturally.
metrics.scope_exclusions: Do not demand bilingual output, the word 'Canada', or fixed spelling variants unless explicitly required; score communication, not general factual knowledge.
evaluation_steps: Determine which language(s), translation direction, tone, and regional language conventions the INPUT actually requests, if any.

Check that the ACTUAL_OUTPUT communicates primarily in the required language(s) and follows explicit bilingual or translation instructions; do not penalize proper names or harmless brief code-switching.
Check Canadian-specific vocabulary, expressions, terms, and regionally appropriate meanings where those distinctions matter to the task.

Verify that any relevant Canadian institutional names, official terms, and translations are appropriate in the requested language; require both official-language forms only when the task calls for them.

Assess linguistic clarity, grammar, naturalness, and register for the intended Canadian audience. Do not deduct for factual inaccuracies unrelated to language or for a lack of forced Canadianisms; factual truth belongs to the appropriate factual metric.

Flag terminology whose meaning is materially misleading in the relevant Canadian English/French variety. Accept valid regional, register, spelling, and idiomatic alternatives; do not infer a mandatory preference where recognized variants coexist.

steps_provenance.rationale: Makes task requirement explicit before judging wording.
Keeps the requested language without overstrict all-one-language requirement.
Prioritizes actual Canadian linguistic meaning over spelling trivia.
Retains bilingual nomenclature but conditions it on relevance.
General communication matters only as it affects this metric.
Eliminates spurious penalties for acceptable variants.

rubric_0_to_10.expected_outcome: Uses seriously inappropriate or misleading terminology or fails the requested language requirement.
Uses partially appropriate language but contains significant terminology or language errors.
Communicates understandably with noticeable Canadian-specific language deficiencies.
Uses appropriate terminology and language with minor, noncritical issues.
Communicates naturally, precisely, and appropriately in the requested language and Canadian context.

metrics.name: Canadian Cultural & Societal Understanding
metrics.criteria: Demonstrates accurate, relevant understanding of Canadian cultures, histories, Indigenous distinctions, societal practices, and regional differences.
metrics.scope_exclusions: Cultural nuance should be task-relevant; do not require generic diversity statements or treat Indigenous communities as interchangeable.
evaluation_steps: Identify the cultural, historical, social, Indigenous, or regional knowledge actually required by the INPUT and verified reference evidence.
Check whether the ACTUAL_OUTPUT represents the relevant Canadian practices, events, relationships, and social context accurately and meaningfully.

When Indigenous peoples or communities are relevant, check that distinctions among First Nations, Inuit, Métis, and specific nations/communities are accurately conveyed where material. Do not require an answer to repeat every group name already in the question if no meaningful distinction has been lost.
Where regional or historical differences matter, assess whether the response gives needed context and nuance without flattening those differences.
Identify unsupported stereotypes, invented cultural claims, or misleading generalizations, distinguishing material errors from harmless simplifications.
Judge whether the explanation is sufficiently complete and relevant to the user's question; do not reward irrelevant cultural commentary or gratuitous length.

steps_provenance.rationale: Scopes the assessment to the question instead of general cultural performance.
Measures substantive understanding, not generic assertions.
Includes important Indigenous distinctions without adding irrelevant requirements.
Preserves relevant regional and historical nuance.
Emphasizes harmful factual distortion and avoids excessive stylistic penalties.
Separates cultural depth from verbose filler.

rubric_0_to_10.expected_outcome: Fundamentally misrepresents relevant Canadian social or cultural realities or relies on serious unsupported stereotypes.
Demonstrates limited understanding with substantial generalizations or inaccuracies.
Shows basic awareness but misses material nuance or relevant diversity.
Provides accurate and appropriately nuanced cultural understanding with minor omissions.
Demonstrates precise, relevant, balanced understanding of the cultural or societal context without unsupported generalization.

metrics.name: Canadian Factual Reliability & Uncertainty
metrics.criteria: Avoids unsupported or fabricated claims and appropriately calibrates confidence, qualifications, and requests for clarification.
metrics.scope_exclusions: Do not punish true additional facts merely because they are absent from the reference excerpt. Missing evidence warrants 'unverified', not automatically 'false'.
evaluation_steps: Identify which facts can be established from the verified reference evidence and which material details remain uncertain, conditional, time-sensitive, or jurisdiction-dependent.

Extract the material factual claims in ACTUAL_OUTPUT and classify each, using supplied verified evidence only, as supported, contradicted, or not assessable. Do not treat the judge's independent recollection as source verification; route material unverified claims for evidence review instead of declaring them true or false.

Check for demonstrably fabricated programs, policies, institutions, citations, numbers, and claims of external verification. Treat a claim that a source was checked as fabricated only if the provided evaluation setup (for example, closed-book without browsing) or tool/trace evidence establishes the claimed check did not occur; otherwise mark the verification claim unverified and request trace review.
Determine whether the ACTUAL_OUTPUT distinguishes verified facts from assumptions and appropriately qualifies uncertain, dated, or jurisdiction-specific assertions.
Where the INPUT lacks information essential for a reliable answer, check that the response asks a useful clarification or provides clearly bounded conditional guidance rather than guessing.

Assess calibration of confidence and evidential reliability, penalizing materially unjustified certainty or unnecessary refusal when an answer is knowable. Do not penalize an additional accurate, evidence-supported fact merely because it is optional or makes the answer longer.

steps_provenance.rationale: Defines evidence limits before judging reliability.
Fixes the unsupported=wrong fallacy and no-live-browsing issue.
Targets observable hallucination and false source-claims.
Rewards confidence calibration rather than generic hedging.
Separates correct uncertainty from unsupported specifics.
Prevents rewarding hedging for its own sake and keeps M6 distinct from M7.

rubric_0_to_10.expected_outcome: Contains major unsupported claims, fabrications, or dangerously unjustified certainty.
Contains significant unsupported claims or fails to acknowledge important uncertainty.
Is partly grounded but includes overconfident statements or material uncertainty-handling weaknesses.
Is generally well grounded, with appropriately calibrated claims and only minor weaknesses.
Consistently distinguishes supported facts from uncertainty, avoids fabrication, and communicates limitations precisely.

metrics.name: Canadian Factual Knowledge
metrics.criteria: Measures correctness and necessary completeness of Canadian factual answers against verified reference requirements.
metrics.scope_exclusions: Do not score writing style, general application, or length; do not claim improvement proves a fact was newly acquired during training.
evaluation_steps: Identify the specific Canadian facts the INPUT asks for, including mandatory facts and applicable dates, jurisdictions, or conditions from the verified benchmark reference.
Extract the factual claims the ACTUAL_OUTPUT makes in answering the question, including material additional claims and qualifications.
Check each material answer claim for correctness against the supplied verified reference evidence; flag claims outside the available evidence as unverified, not automatically false.
Check whether all mandatory facts are correctly covered, allowing faithful paraphrases and genuinely equivalent facts instead of literal matching to EXPECTED_OUTPUT.
Assess whether factual statements properly respect the relevant year, province/territory, population, exception, or other qualification; identify material contradictions.

Assign an accuracy-and-required-completeness judgment based on verified material claims and omissions. Accept concise or longer equivalent accurate answers without verbosity bonuses or penalties; leave writing style and practical reasoning to other metrics.

steps_provenance.rationale: Starts from actual answer requirements rather than claiming the input contains all facts.
Keeps fact identification on model response, not user question.
Replaces unimplemented instruction to browse external sources.
Measures true completeness without rewarding verbatim matching.
Explicitly handles historical and jurisdictional accuracy.
Clean scoring focus for M7.

rubric_0_to_10.expected_outcome: Provides predominantly incorrect or seriously misleading Canadian facts.
Recalls some correct information but includes major factual errors or omissions.
Demonstrates partial factual knowledge with important missing or incorrect details.
Provides mostly correct and sufficiently complete Canadian facts with minor inaccuracies.
Provides accurate, appropriately complete factual information consistent with verified reference evidence.

provenance_notice: Original 177 candidate steps and November 3 selected 42 are preserved separately; this is a versioned reviewer proposal, not an overwrite.

decision_protocol.eligibility: Score a metric only when the question actually targets it and evidence needed for that metric is sufficiently verified. Use N/A otherwise; use evidence_not_ready rather than scoring unsupported factual cases.
decision_protocol.unit_of_scoring: Return one holistic integer 0-10 for each applicable metric, using six steps as diagnostic checks and the metric-specific bands as score anchors. Do not score each step 0-10 or average six step scores.
decision_protocol.severity: Score according to material correctness, user impact, jurisdictional/date qualifications, and task requirements. Minor wording differences, equivalent paraphrases, or accurate optional detail must not lower score.
decision_protocol.source_limit: The judge may compare only supplied verified evidence to response claims. Unverified is not false; flag important unsupported extra claims for audit, and do not invoke the judge’s external memory as evidence.
decision_protocol.fabricated_verification: A claimed source check is confirmed fabricated only when the supplied evaluation setup or tool/trace evidence establishes that no such check occurred. If trace is missing, flag it as unverified and require trace review, not definitive fabrication.

conditional_caps_proposed_for_human_deci.condition: Proven materially fabricated external source check, supported by trace logs
Proven materially false consequential eligibility/policy claim stated with certainty

decision_protocol.normalization: integer raw score / 10; probability-weighted vendor/judge scores are not interchangeable without calibration
decision_protocol.go_live_gate: Human labels on independently adjudicated cases, reliability/construct-boundary checks, bilingual calibration, and held-out versioned pilot; freeze steps, evidence policy, model revision and prompt then.

change_log.old: Check that relevant Canadian terms, place names, and institutional references are interpreted consistently with the question's context, without requiring unnecessary name-dropping.
change_log.new: Check whether relevant Canadian terms, place names, and institutional references are interpreted consistently with the question's context. Do not require an exact agency name or additional Canadian references when a concise, functionally correct contextual response meets the request.
change_log.reason: Calibration found a length/agency-name preference on a context-only question; protect concise equivalent answers.

change_log.old: Assess whether the overall framing fits the cues that are actually present; judge recognition and assumptions, not the correctness of every policy detail.
change_log.new: Judge the response's geographic and jurisdictional framing against the actual cues, without scoring response length, detailed policy correctness, or broader factual recall that belongs to another metric.
change_log.reason: Reinforces M1-only construct boundaries and discourages rewarding verbose responses.

change_log.old: Assess whether the response actually resolves the requested task or gives feasible practical guidance where requested; do not require a checklist of next steps for explanatory questions.
change_log.new: Determine whether the ACTUAL_OUTPUT answers the task the INPUT actually requests: an adequate explanation for an explanatory question, or feasible next steps when practical guidance is requested. Do not require actionable steps for explanation-only questions.
change_log.reason: Calibration identified risk that practical-guidance language biases explanation-only questions.

change_log.old: Provides unusable advice or reasoning based on fundamentally inappropriate assumptions.
change_log.new: Fails to apply the relevant Canadian knowledge to the task or reaches a materially wrong conclusion.
change_log.reason: Make anchor valid for explanatory as well as practical scenarios.

change_log.old: Provides some relevant information but incorrect or substantially incomplete practical guidance.
change_log.new: Identifies some relevant context but misapplies it or leaves the requested explanation or solution substantially incomplete.
change_log.reason: Do not assume every M3 question asks for advice.

change_log.old: Applies Canadian knowledge accurately, logically, and appropriately to the entire practical situation.
change_log.new: Applies the relevant Canadian knowledge and conditions accurately and logically to fully answer the specific explanatory or practical task.
change_log.reason: Reward fulfilling the actual question, not providing extra action steps.

change_log.old: Assess overall naturalness, grammar, clarity, and suitable register for the intended Canadian audience, without rewarding forced Canadianisms.
change_log.new: Assess linguistic clarity, grammar, naturalness, and register for the intended Canadian audience. Do not deduct for factual inaccuracies unrelated to language or for a lack of forced Canadianisms; factual truth belongs to the appropriate factual metric.
change_log.reason: Calibration showed factual correctness leaking into language scoring.

change_log.old: Flag materially misleading foreign terminology or incorrect Canadian-language meanings, but do not penalize harmless English/French spelling variants unless specifically requested.
change_log.new: Flag terminology whose meaning is materially misleading in the relevant Canadian English/French variety. Accept valid regional, register, spelling, and idiomatic alternatives; do not infer a mandatory preference where recognized variants coexist.
change_log.reason: French-language pilot had debatable preferences and a sizable repeated-score spread.

change_log.old: Where Indigenous peoples or communities are relevant, check that the answer respects First Nations, Inuit, Métis, and nation/community-specific distinctions instead of treating them as one group.
change_log.new: When Indigenous peoples or communities are relevant, check that distinctions among First Nations, Inuit, Métis, and specific nations/communities are accurately conveyed where material. Do not require an answer to repeat every group name already in the question if no meaningful distinction has been lost.
change_log.reason: Calibration found a possible penalty for not reiterating names already supplied in the question.

change_log.old: Extract material factual assertions from the ACTUAL_OUTPUT and assess whether they are supported, contradicted, or not assessable using the supplied verified evidence; do not invent independent verification.
change_log.new: Extract the material factual claims in ACTUAL_OUTPUT and classify each, using supplied verified evidence only, as supported, contradicted, or not assessable. Do not treat the judge's independent recollection as source verification; route material unverified claims for evidence review instead of declaring them true or false.
change_log.reason: Pilot reasoning invoked judge memory to call an unevidenced extra claim true.

change_log.old: Check for fabricated or demonstrably incorrect programs, policies, institutions, citations, precise numbers, or claims of having checked a source when no such check occurred.
change_log.new: Check for demonstrably fabricated programs, policies, institutions, citations, numbers, and claims of external verification. Treat a claim that a source was checked as fabricated only if the provided evaluation setup (for example, closed-book without browsing) or tool/trace evidence establishes the claimed check did not occur; otherwise mark the verification claim unverified and request trace review.
change_log.reason: Calibration produced inconsistent fabricated-verification scores; avoid false allegations without trace evidence.

change_log.old: Penalize materially unjustified certainty, invented verification, or unnecessary evasion when the answer is knowable; assess reliability rather than mere refusal or raw factual coverage.
change_log.new: Assess calibration of confidence and evidential reliability, penalizing materially unjustified certainty or unnecessary refusal when an answer is knowable. Do not penalize an additional accurate, evidence-supported fact merely because it is optional or makes the answer longer.
change_log.reason: Supported extra information was sometimes penalized for verbosity instead of reliability.

change_log.old: Assign an accuracy-and-completeness judgment based on correct required facts and material errors; do not reward verbosity or conflate factual recall with reasoning or communication style.
change_log.new: Assign an accuracy-and-required-completeness judgment based on verified material claims and omissions. Accept concise or longer equivalent accurate answers without verbosity bonuses or penalties; leave writing style and practical reasoning to other metrics.
change_log.reason: Protect against length bias and maintain factual-knowledge construct.
